I recently brewed a strawberry rhubarb soda but fermentation was very slow to get started and I could smell an 'off' smell in the wort. Rather than bottle it to carbonate and trap the bad smell, I added zinc to help the yeast along (zinc is often the cure for a stuck fermentation indicating yeast malnutrition) and decided to go for a wine instead.

Since it was intended as a soda, I was concerned that the sugar content would be way too high, but my hydrometer indicated that it would ferment out to about 5% ABV, which was surprising, considering there's at least 10% sugar by weight in there. I'm undecided if I want the end product to be dry or sweet; it *is* strawberry which is almost always a sweet flavour. I'll probably let it ferment dry but I'm tempted to bottle it (in soda bottles) before fermentation finishes and carbonate it at the same time.

Since brewing this I've learned that lots of winemakers don't boil their flavour components because that causes pectin extraction. This brew definitely has a pectin haze going on, but apart from the insane head retention (foam for days, hence the inaccuracy of the ABV measure) I don't mind the haze. The colour is an amazingly vibrant red.

This is my first attempt at an alcoholic homebrew, so it will be interesting to see how it turns out.
